item.title: Aspen Global Change Institute: Climate and Environment Data Stewardship Fellow
item.description:
Organisation: Aspen Global Change Institute (AGCI), with Public Environmental Data Partners

Location: Remote anywhere within the continental United States. AGCI's primary office is in Basalt, Colorado, under an 'Institute Without Walls' approach. Travel: up to 8 domestic trips a year and up to 1 international trip.

Award: Anticipated salary USD 85,000 to 100,000, based on the general US market.

Duration: Full-time for 1 year; start as soon as possible and no later than 1 October 2026

Deadline: Closed 19 Aug 2026

AGCI is hiring a Climate and Environment Data Stewardship Fellow to coordinate and contribute to cross-organizational climate and environmental data stewardship efforts, supporting synergies and collective learning across established initiatives and networks focused on the collection and management of data used to inform climate action, in ways that promote long-term data quality, accessibility, interoperability and security. PLACEMENT AND MENTORSHIP: the fellow sits within AGCI's Engaged Research Team, reporting to AGCI's Research Director, with day-to-day mentorship from leaders at core partner organisations in the data stewardship space, including the Data Foundation (Sonia Wang) and Public Environmental Data Partners' co-founding member the Open Environmental Data Project (Brittany Janis), plus guidance from other leaders in the field. RESPONSIBILITIES: coordination of the coordinators, using a network-of-networks approach to build connectedness across emerging and existing work in the climate and environmental data landscape and to help the network identify and act on shared priorities; planning and coordinating network meetings, workshops and other convenings, starting with consolidating the landscape analysis exercises already underway; elevating data stewardship work by developing and sharing a comprehensive picture of what is needed to sustain data critical to climate action; supporting peer learning through surveys, focus groups or scenario planning that enable cross-organisation conversations about possible futures; connecting evolving data stewardship to the broader climate action and investment ecosystem; and contributing to the Climate Reserve, including professional development programming alongside other Climate Reserve-supported fellows. REQUIREMENTS: bachelor's degree required, master's or doctorate preferred; minimum 3 years managing communities of practice (working groups, interagency groups and similar) or coordinating multi-organisation or network-based initiatives, ideally related to climate or environmental science or policy; familiarity with data stewardship principles (long-term data quality, accessibility, interoperability, security) sufficient to support conversations across technical and non-technical partners; public speaking experience; experience working across institutional, sectoral and geographic contexts at the science-policy interface; strong project management, research, analysis and synthesis skills; and willingness to travel domestically and internationally. Domain expertise in any one data stewardship area is not required, and knowledge of the civil society data stewardship space is desirable rather than expected. TERM AND PAY: full-time for one year at an anticipated USD 85,000 to 100,000. DEADLINE: priority deadline 19 August 2026. HOW TO APPLY: through the AGCI Workable posting.

item.title: Microsoft: Applied Scientist II / Senior Applied Scientist, Responsible AI (CoreAI)
item.description:
Organisation: Microsoft, CoreAI Platform and Tools (Responsible AI team)

Location: Redmond, Washington, USA (the posting lists four further locations), 3 days per week in office. Travel under 25 percent.

Award: Two levels are open. Applied Sciences IC3: typical US base pay USD 102,100 to 202,200 per year (USD 133,800 to 219,200 in the San Francisco Bay Area and New York City metro). Applied Sciences IC4: USD 119,800 to 234,700 per year (USD 160,200 to 261,000 in those metros). Certain roles are eligible for benefits and additional compensation. Full-time individual contributor.

Duration: Full-time, permanent. Applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled (posted 10 July 2026, job number 200017828).

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The Responsible AI team inside Microsoft's CoreAI Platform and Tools organisation is hiring at two levels (Applied Scientist II and Senior Applied Scientist) to build the RAI service components used across Microsoft's AI products by hundreds of millions of people. RESPONSIBILITIES: supervised fine-tuning of LLMs including reinforcement learning from human feedback, with thorough evaluation; working with the tech lead on the design and implementation of agent adversarial evaluations and safety mitigations so that agent creators can identify risks and apply safeguards; and collaborating with the RAI engineering team to ship those mitigations at scale, refine them against operational performance and resolve end-to-end issues. REQUIRED: a Bachelor's in computer science, computational linguistics or a related field plus 2+ years of related experience, OR a Master's plus 1+ year, OR a Doctorate, OR equivalent experience. Candidates must pass the Microsoft Cloud background check on hire and every two years after. PREFERRED: a Master's plus 6+ years or a Doctorate plus 3+ years; 2 to 3+ years owning feature design, model development, evaluation and deployment; strong machine learning background especially NLP and deep learning; language model training and evaluation experience; Responsible AI research experience; Python and C# with PyTorch and Triton; large-scale data processing; unit testing, TDD and DevOps practice; platform and API design, debugging and data analysis; full-stack (client to service) development is a plus. Posted 10 July 2026 (job number 200017828); open for a minimum of 5 days and then until filled.

item.title: Microsoft: AI Security Researcher II, AI Red Team
item.description:
Organisation: Microsoft Security (AI Red Team)

Location: Redmond, Washington, USA, 3 days per week in office; the team states it is open to remote work. Travel under 25 percent.

Award: Applied Sciences IC3: typical US base pay USD 102,100 to 202,200 per year; USD 133,800 to 219,200 in the San Francisco Bay Area and New York City metropolitan area. Certain roles are eligible for benefits and additional compensation. Full-time individual contributor.

Duration: Full-time, permanent. Applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled (posted 29 July 2026, job number 200045204).

Deadline: Rolling / undated

A research role on Microsoft's AI Red Team, an interdisciplinary group of researchers, red teamers and engineers working to understand and reduce security risks in Microsoft's AI systems, with impact across the Phi series, Bing Copilot, Security Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Office Copilot, Windows Copilot and Azure OpenAI. The brief is agent security: how autonomous, tool-using and multi-agent systems fail, and what principled methods can evaluate and improve them. RESPONSIBILITIES: formulate and investigate research questions at the intersection of cybersecurity and agentic AI behaviour, covering security risks, failure modes and adversarial behaviour; design rigorous experiments, evaluations and benchmarks for autonomous, tool-using and multi-agent systems; develop research insights, methodologies and mitigations; and work with product teams to turn findings into practical security improvements. REQUIRED: a Bachelor's in statistics, econometrics, computer science, electrical or computer engineering or a related field plus 2+ years of related research experience, OR a Master's plus 1+ year, OR a Doctorate, OR equivalent experience. Candidates must be able to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check on hire and every two years after. PREFERRED: demonstrated research output in AI security, adversarial machine learning, agentic systems or LLM evaluation (publications, preprints, technical reports, talks, open-source tools or research artifacts); experience designing experiments, evaluations, benchmarks or methodologies for security-relevant behaviour in AI systems; comfort in an interdisciplinary team; and the ability to connect findings to practical security guidance for shipped products. Posted 29 July 2026 (job number 200045204); open for a minimum of 5 days and then until filled, so apply early. Background on the team's approach: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2023/08/07/microsoft-ai-red-team-building-future-of-safer-ai/

item.title: ProPublica Emerging Reporters Program 2026-2027
item.description:
Organisation: ProPublica

Location: Remote, with an all-expenses-paid trip to a journalism conference. RESTRICTED: US citizens or US residents only, and participants must supply a completed W-9 with a valid SSN or ITIN (no exceptions).

Award: $9,000 stipend, paid as two instalments of $4,500 (one at the start of the programme, one at the midpoint), plus a fully funded journalism conference trip with accommodation and expenses covered. No application fee.

Duration: Late September 2026 through June 2027, remote

Deadline: Closed 17 Aug 2026

ProPublica's Emerging Reporters Program is a remote mentorship and professional-development programme for aspiring investigative journalists, built specifically for students for whom investigative journalism is financially out of reach. Five students are selected each year. WHAT FELLOWS RECEIVE: a $9,000 stipend paid in two $4,500 instalments (start and midpoint), one-to-one mentoring from ProPublica journalists, training and resources, and an all-expenses-paid trip to a journalism conference such as the Investigative Reporters and Editors conference (accommodation and expenses covered by ProPublica). ELIGIBILITY: undergraduate juniors or seniors enrolled during the 2026-27 academic year, who can demonstrate financial need and early dedication to journalism through internships, campus publications or local news work. Students from groups traditionally underrepresented in journalism are especially encouraged to apply. HARD RESTRICTION: applicants must be US citizens or US residents and able to file US taxes; the required W-9 needs a valid Social Security number or ITIN, and ProPublica states it makes no exceptions. APPLICATION: resume or CV, current academic transcript, expected graduation date, essays on investigative-journalism interest, career goals, financial circumstances and barriers faced, plus three journalism projects with URLs or PDFs and a backstory of up to 200 words each. Applications close 17 August 2026 at 9:00am ET.

item.title: Trusted Creator Fellowship 2026 (News Creator Corps)
item.description:
Organisation: News Creator Corps (a project of the Good Information Foundation)

Location: Virtual, meeting once a week. RESTRICTED: US-based creators only.

Award: $5,000 stipend on completing the programme. No application fee.

Duration: Roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026, virtual sessions once a week

Deadline: Closed 17 Aug 2026

A short-term virtual fellowship from News Creator Corps that trains independent content creators in the tactical craft of journalism: fact-checking, sourcing and interviewing, applied directly to their own channels during the programme so the community they already serve gets more credible information. WHO IT IS FOR: independent creators with an engaged following on digital platforms (Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, Substack, YouTube and similar) whose content is information-based and serves a specific community. It is explicitly not aimed at traditional journalists already trained in reporting fundamentals. STUDENT SEATS: three places in the autumn cohort are reserved for full-time college students aged 25 or younger, who get the same fellowship experience as everyone else. WHAT FELLOWS RECEIVE: a $5,000 stipend on completion, weekly virtual sessions, and access to discussion forums with the cohort, trainers, staff and alumni. ELIGIBILITY: US-based only. KEY DATES: applications close 17 August 2026 at 11:59pm ET; notifications by the end of September 2026; programme runs roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026. Contact: creatorprogram@newscreatorcorps.org. Sibling programme to the Rural Creator Fellowship.

item.title: Beinecke Library Short-Term Research Fellowships 2027-2028 (Yale)
item.description:
Organisation: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale University

Location: Onsite at Yale Library Special Collections, New Haven, Connecticut, USA. Open to academic and independent scholars locally and globally, regardless of institutional association.

Award: USD 5,000 per month for research visits between two weeks and two months. Funding is paid at the beginning of the fellowship where possible (payment to international fellows often takes several weeks); fellows are responsible for taxes on the award. Free to apply.

Duration: Two weeks to two months of onsite research, conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028; awards cannot be deferred

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

The Beinecke Library Fellowship Program offers competitive short-term fellowships to support research projects that substantively engage with Yale Library Special Collections materials. WHO CAN APPLY: academic and independent scholars, locally and globally, with or without an institutional affiliation; the library explicitly welcomes applicants regardless of institutional association, race, cultural background, ability, sexual orientation, gender or socioeconomic status. Applications using traditional archival and bibliographic research methods are encouraged, and so are creative, interdisciplinary and non-traditional approaches to working with the collections, which makes this a live option for artists and writers whose practice is research-driven. WHAT YOU GET: USD 5,000 per month for an onsite research visit of between two weeks and two months, paid at the start of the fellowship whenever possible (international fellows should expect payment to take several weeks); fellows pay their own taxes on the award. TIMELINE: applications for the 2027-2028 awards opened 1 June 2026 and close 15 August 2026, via Interfolio; all decisions are notified by 31 January 2027; research must be conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028, and awards cannot be deferred.

item.title: Transfyr AI Fellowship 2026-2027 (Boston/Cambridge)
item.description:
Organisation: Transfyr

Location: Boston/Cambridge, Massachusetts, US, full-time in person. Remote considered by exception when the project and candidate make it workable.

Award: $125,000 annual compensation plus benefits, plus access to compute, GPUs, data and project support. Applicants are asked to specify the compute, GPU, data or support their project would need. No application fee.

Duration: Full-time for 12 months

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

A one-year, full-time research fellowship for graduate students, recent PhDs and postdocs to lead a project on frontier machine learning problems grounded in how scientific work actually happens. THE PREMISE: Transfyr argues science is missing an observability layer. Lab work is full of tacit decisions, failed attempts, operator judgment, noisy instruments and context that never reaches the written protocol, and the company is building what it calls the world's largest multimodal dataset of scientific execution for models to reason over. Fellows get to work with that data. RESEARCH AGENDA, eight named directions: multimodal reasoning (aligning video, audio, protocol text, instrument traces, timestamps, gaze and outcomes); conflicting evidence (uncertainty and calibration, evidence attribution, contradiction-aware reasoning); long-context scientific memory (long-horizon state tracking, retrieval over process histories, failure and deviation memory); real-world evaluations (benchmark design, process-level metrics, lab-grounded model assessment); tacit expertise (expert-novice comparison, skill representation, human-in-the-loop feedback); physical-world AI (embodied data pipelines, transfer across settings, policy and assistance evaluation); biosecurity and bio-risk observability (synthesis-to-execution verification, emergent capability tracking, autonomous vulnerability detection); and scientific execution ontology (wet-lab-grounded metadata design, cross-domain causal attribution, multi-scale variability mapping). WHAT FELLOWS DO: define a research question, build prototypes, analyse real multimodal scientific-execution data, pressure-test evaluation ideas, and produce a publishable or demo-grade artifact, with direct mentorship from Transfyr's founders, technical team and advisor network across AI, biology, robotics and scientific operations. WHO CAN APPLY: current graduate students able to take leave (and to self-certify that they can commit full-time), recent PhDs and postdocs in machine learning, computer science, computational biology, robotics, human-computer interaction, statistics or adjacent fields. Strong ML fundamentals and evidence of research taste are the bar; the call asks for comfort with ambiguity and curiosity about how science happens in physical environments. International applicants are welcome and visa support is available for selected fellows. IP TERMS, worth reading before applying: Transfyr owns the fellowship work product and supports publication subject to confidentiality and IP review. This is a company fellowship, not an academic one. APPLICATION: a one-page application sent to ai_fellowship@transfyr.ai saying what you want to work on and what resources you need, with links that make your work easy to evaluate; references are requested of finalists. DEADLINE: applications are reviewed on a ROLLING basis; apply by 15 August 2026 for full consideration, decisions roll through late August 2026, fellowship begins around September 2026.

item.title: Science & Technology Policy Fellowships, 2027-28 Class
item.description:
Organisation: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

Location: Washington DC, USA. Fellows are placed in US federal executive, legislative and judicial branch offices and must reside in the DC area.

Award: Stipend depending on experience and placement, roughly USD 85,000 to 140,000; the dedicated AI legislative branch cohort is paid at GS-12 Step 10 on the DC locality scale. Includes health insurance, a travel and professional development allowance, and relocation support for some placements. No application fee.

Duration: One year, 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028, renewable in some placements

Deadline: 01 Nov 2026

The AAAS Science & Technology Policy Fellowships place scientists and engineers inside US federal agencies, congressional offices and the judicial branch for a year of hands-on policymaking, contributing technical knowledge and analytical skills to the federal policy process. AI, data and computing policy placements are among the largest tracks, and AAAS runs a dedicated AI legislative branch cohort that places AI experts in congressional offices at GS-12 Step 10 on the DC locality scale. ELIGIBILITY: US citizens holding a PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in any science or engineering field, or a master's degree in engineering plus three years of post-degree professional experience; some tracks accept a bachelor's plus five years. Relevant expertise includes AI, machine learning, computer science, robotics and data science. Fellows must reside in DC, Maryland or northern Virginia during the fellowship year. TIMELINE: the application portal opens 1 August 2026 and closes 1 November 2026 at 11:59pm ET, with eligibility notification in late November, interview notification January to February 2027, semi-finalist interviews in March, placement offers by early May, and the fellowship year running 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028. Apply through fellowshipapp.aaas.org.

item.title: Horizon Fellowship, 2027 Cohort
item.description:
Organisation: Horizon Institute for Public Service

Location: Washington DC, USA (residence required for placement). Part-time remote training January to March 2027.

Award: Base salary of USD 78,000 for junior fellows, USD 130,000 for fellows, and USD 190,000 or more for senior fellows, plus a USD 17,000 benefits stipend, a USD 3,000 professional development stipend, and up to USD 3,000 relocation assistance. No application fee.

Duration: 6 months for junior fellows, 12 months for fellows and senior fellows, with potential renewal. Part-time remote training January to March 2027, matching April to May 2027, placement from summer 2027.

Deadline: 30 Aug 2026

The Horizon Fellowship places technologists, scientists and researchers with emerging-technology expertise into US federal agencies, congressional offices and Washington DC think tanks to work on AI, biotechnology and emerging-technology policy. The 2027 cohort runs three tiers: junior fellows (under three years of experience, no PhD) at a USD 78,000 base for six months; fellows (three or more years of relevant experience, or a PhD) at USD 130,000 for twelve months; and a newly added senior fellow tier (twelve or more years of experience with a leadership background) at USD 190,000 or more for twelve months. All tiers receive a USD 17,000 benefits stipend, a USD 3,000 professional development stipend and up to USD 3,000 in relocation assistance, and all are potentially renewable. The programme year begins with part-time remote training from January to March 2027, followed by matching in April and May and placement from spring or summer 2027 onward. Most offers are expected by the end of November 2026. Placements run up to two years in total: fellows and senior fellows take a one-year term at a federal agency, congressional office or think tank with the option to renew for a second one-year term, potentially on a different institutional track, while junior think tank fellows take a six-month term renewable once. Horizon reports that nearly all finalists across its five cohorts to date have secured a placement at a host organization. WHAT THE FELLOWSHIP INCLUDES: dedicated training on the policy landscape and applied skills such as writing and policy analysis; a tight-knit peer community; introductions to host offices central to US emerging technology policy; and mentorship from senior leaders and the broader Horizon community. ELIGIBILITY: no prior policy experience or specific degree is required, and Horizon explicitly welcomes candidates from diverse backgrounds; fellows must reside in the Washington DC area for the placement. WORK AUTHORISATION: applicants need pre-existing work authorisation that does not depend on employer sponsorship. Non-US citizens on E-3, TN or H-1B1 visas may qualify case by case; F-1 OPT during the first year after graduation is acceptable but STEM OPT extensions are not; green card holders are eligible but may face restrictions on executive branch roles. Junior fellows have no specific degree requirement and may apply while finishing college, but are limited to the think tank track. SELECTION PROCESS (September to November 2026): application decision, then a paid work sample of up to 6 hours, a 20-minute screening interview, a 40-minute technical interview and a 25-minute final interview. Applications close 30 August 2026 at 11:59pm Anywhere on Earth.

item.title: Good Life Residents Program: AI and Finance
item.description:
Organisation: Roosevelt Institute, in partnership with Data & Society

Location: Remote. Travel may be requested for select convenings and for the culminating public event. US economic policy focus.

Award: USD 3,000 stipend, plus travel and accommodation for the culminating event if needed. No application fee.

Duration: 6 months, part-time at roughly 5 to 8 hours per month

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The Good Life Residents Program is a six-month Roosevelt Institute initiative that develops new leaders and elevates bold ideas across six economic policy priorities under its Good Life Agenda. Each topic area hosts a cohort of 3 to 4 residents plus 1 to 2 senior Topic Advisors (academics, policy leaders, organizers or government practitioners) who provide strategic and intellectual mentorship and moderate the closing event. Residents write a roughly 1,500-word original policy essay advancing a people-centered policy vision against a topic-specific prompt, take part in structured dialogue with peers, Topic Advisors and Roosevelt Think Tank directors, help prepare and appear at a culminating public event, contribute to press opportunities such as op-eds and reporter calls where applicable, and act as ambassadors for the Good Life Agenda in their professional and public networks. The current round, the AI and Finance Residents Program, is run in partnership with Data & Society and asks for bold ideas on how to shape, redirect, interrupt or make more visible and contestable the flows of capital into generative AI. Framing: breakneck investment in generative AI technology and infrastructure is distorting the stock market, profit measures, bond issuance, the pace and composition of growth, job creation and trade policy, with seven tech companies accounting for more than a third of S&P 500 market capitalisation and complex, sometimes circular financial arrangements obscuring risk. Suggested lines of inquiry include what government interventions could improve public oversight, risk allocation and direction-setting in private markets; how other investments could be coordinated and scaled if AI spending is crowding them out; what role public spending or new institutions could play in catalysing technology R&D designed to support workers, sustainability and supply chains; what democratic input mechanisms would keep state influence over capital flows less vulnerable to corruption; and how federal AI policy should address public hostility to data centre investments alongside national security and competitiveness. Compensation is USD 3,000 plus travel and accommodation for the culminating event. FLAG: Roosevelt does not publish an application deadline for the AI and Finance round on the programme page, and earlier rounds (Social Security financing, Federal Reserve powers, housing) each ran their own short application window. Check the Formstack application form linked from the programme page for the current closing date before applying.

item.title: Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) Fellowship
item.description:
Organisation: RAND Corporation, Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST)

Location: Washington DC, San Francisco or Pittsburgh, USA, or remote within the United States; fellows may also be based in the United Kingdom

Award: US fellows: annual stipend from USD 40,000 to 200,000 for full-time fellows depending on experience, plus a monthly payment usable for health and dental insurance. UK fellows: compensation based on experience. No application fee.

Duration: Typically starts at 6 months, extendable up to 3 years; full-time or part-time

Deadline: Closed 01 Aug 2026

RAND's Center on AI, Security, and Technology (CAST) runs a rolling fellowship for researchers working on AI security and technology policy, with mentorship from RAND policy experts. Fellows can be based in Washington DC, San Francisco or Pittsburgh, work remotely within the United States, or be based in the United Kingdom. Terms are flexible: engagements typically start at six months and can be extended up to three years, full-time or part-time. US fellows receive an annual stipend ranging from USD 40,000 to 200,000 for full-time work depending on experience, plus a monthly payment that can be put toward health and dental insurance; UK fellows are compensated based on experience. The programme spans career stages from undergraduate through mid-career. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be based in the US or UK; US applicants need to be eligible for a government security clearance, and UK applicants must have a current and ongoing right to work in the UK. Current RAND staff are not eligible. ROLLING DEADLINE: applications are submitted through an online form and reviewed quarterly, with published cutoffs of 1 February, 1 May, 1 August and 1 November, each answered by the first of the following month. The date recorded here is the next cutoff (1 August 2026); the call does not close after it. RAND notes that if one of its listed staff openings matches your interest you should apply to that instead, and suggests not applying to the fellowship if you have submitted another CAST application within the last six months.

item.title: Law & AI Academic Fellowship
item.description:
Organisation: Institute for Law & AI (LawAI)

Location: Washington DC, USA; Cambridge, UK; or remote

Award: USD 130,000 annual salary. No application fee.

Duration: Two years, full-time

Deadline: Closed 31 Jul 2026

The Institute for Law & AI (LawAI), an independent think tank researching and advising on the legal challenges posed by artificial intelligence, is running its inaugural Law & AI Academic Fellowship for aspiring legal scholars who intend to go on the US legal academic job market. The fellowship is designed as an alternative to university-sponsored Visiting Assistant Professor or law fellow positions: fellows spend the majority of their time researching and writing articles for publication in law journals on the law of transformative AI, and are prepared for the academic job market as part of a larger application package. Teaching is not required, which LawAI frames as a benefit over most university-affiliated positions, though fellows who want teaching experience are encouraged to seek it and LawAI and its affiliates may be able to help secure positions. Each fellow is paired with an academic mentor from LawAI's network of affiliated academics for ongoing support, with more intensive help in the final stages of the job application process including moot interviews and detailed feedback. Fellows may also inquire about spending time in residence at academic institutions of interest. Candidates are selected in part on how well their research interests align with LawAI's: the institute expects AI to reshape culture, the economy, public policy, public administration, politics, military affairs and geostrategy at least as profoundly as the Industrial Revolution, and asks whether a candidate's research is well-scoped to changes of that magnitude. Areas of particular interest include risk regulation of transformative AI, liability for AI harms, AI and biosecurity, AI and cybersecurity, executive branch use of transformative AI, national security law, law and AI infrastructure, administrative law, constitutional law, international regulation, AI in the judiciary, and industrial policy. Full-time two-year role at USD 130,000 per year, based in Washington DC, Cambridge UK, or remote. Applications close 31 July 2026.

item.title: Senior Researcher, AI Civics
item.description:
Organisation: Data & Society Research Institute

Location: Fully remote within the United States. Data & Society is based in New York City and operates as a remote-first organisation; occasional onsite meetings possible. You must be living and authorised to work in the US; no visa sponsorship.

Award: USD 78,000 to 97,000 annual salary, commensurate with experience, plus medical, dental and vision insurance, opt-in insurance and 401k products, paid time off and paid federal holidays. No application fee.

Duration: Two-year full-time position, September 2026 to 31 May 2028, with no expectation of extension

Deadline: Closed 30 Jul 2026

Data & Society, the independent nonprofit studying the social implications of data-centric technologies and automation, is hiring a Senior Researcher for AI Civics, a newly launched two-year programme on civic action and community control over AI. The programme aims to amplify the tools of civic participation so the public can directly shape the role AI plays in society, surfacing civic tools people can use to exert political power over AI systems and tech platforms at community level. It co-creates toolkits and training resources with anchor partner organisations, diffuses them through a train-the-trainer model, and builds toward a national civic coalition demanding democratic accountability over AI. The Senior Researcher is a subject-matter expert and lead contributor, drawing primarily on participatory methods and especially participatory action research, and is responsible for one or more inter-organisational partnerships with national partner organisations working in K-12 education, labour, faith or advocacy. Responsibilities span cultivating and stewarding relationships with partner staff, community members and leaders and public sector workers; leading collaborative relationships with an anchor partner and its local members for the co-creation and diffusion of AI Civics resources; co-developing and iterating toolkits, facilitation guides and training curricula and running piloting, feedback and revision cycles; producing case studies, educational materials, templates, reports, academic publications, lectures and public writing; supporting facilitation preparation for co-design workshops, train-the-trainer sessions and participatory research activities; developing research questions, strategies and new external partnerships with the Program Director; network communications; participating in fundraising, including grant applications and materials for the Development Team; and contributing to the intellectual life of the organisation. REQUIRED: graduate degree or equivalent; expertise in one or more sectors of interest to the programme (K-12 education, labour, faith groups, or another institutional pillar of civic life as it relates to data-centric technologies and AI); 7 to 10 years minimum experience in research organisations or research environments (university, public policy, advocacy, government), inclusive of graduate work; expertise in participatory research methods; a strong track record of seeing research through to publication; a public profile and ability to reach non-academic audiences through writing and speaking; and the ability to coordinate and conduct in-depth qualitative research.
